parameters.content:
## Two Different Kinds of Webhook, On Purpose
**Check Availability** and **Book Appointment** are LIVE, synchronous tools Vapi calls mid-call and waits on for a response — the caller is on hold for whatever these take, so they call Cal.com directly and return fast. **End of Call** is fire-and-forget: Vapi sends it after the call is already over, so it just logs to Airtable and fires the missed-call SMS with no one waiting on the response (`responseMode: onReceived`).

Both Cal.com HTTP Request nodes use `onError: continueRegularOutput` deliberately — if the calendar API fails mid-call, the workflow doesn't error out and leave the caller in dead air. The formatting step right after checks for that failure and hands the AI a fallback line ("team will call back") instead.

nodes.name: Note: Live Tools vs Post-Call Webhook

parameters.content:
## Parsing Vapi's Payloads Is a First Draft
The exact shape of Vapi's tool-call and end-of-call-report webhooks can shift between API versions, and this was written before seeing a real payload. Every Code node here defaults to safe fallback values (empty strings, 'Missed Call', a generic callback line) rather than throwing, so a schema mismatch degrades gracefully instead of breaking the call — but the field paths (`message.toolCallList`, `message.artifact.messages`) need confirming against a real execution log and adjusting if Vapi's actual structure differs.

## Why the Booking Attendee Email Is Fixed, Not Collected
Cal.com's booking API requires a real, deliverable attendee email, but this workflow deliberately doesn't ask the caller for one. Email is painful to collect over voice (spelling it out, domain confusion) and callers phoning a home-service line don't expect an email exchange the way a webinar signup implies one. The caller's real confirmation is the voice read-back on the call itself, plus their phone number for follow-up — Cal.com's own confirmation email is an internal record, not the customer-facing touchpoint.

For a real client this would be the business's own booking-notifications inbox (e.g. `bookings@clientdomain.com`), not something collected per caller either.
